analysis:
## The dip-buy paid

Five sessions ago the June 10 dossier called the AVGO-driven flush to $200 a buying opportunity with a $195 stop, and said a reclaim of $210 would confirm the dip was bought. Today it happened. NVDA is trading **~$211.02** (range **$207.71–$211.38**), back **above $210** for the first time since the selloff and **~+5% off the $200 add zone**. The $200 level held three times, then resolved up. Bulls won the week; the 'Broadcom misread' thesis was correct.

## The overhang is gone

The catalyst is macro. [Trump announced Sunday the US–Iran peace deal is 'now complete'](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/live/stock-market-today-monday-june-15-224751171.html), the **Strait of Hormuz is reopening**, and **oil is tumbling**. The single regime trigger that justified the early-June caution — the oil/Iran overhang on high-multiple tech — is **cleared**. The broad tape reflects it: [S&P +1.49% to ~7,542](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/6/15/stock-markets-soar-oil-falls-as-us-iran-confirm-deal-to-end-war), back above the 7,460 regime floor, Nasdaq **+2.38%**, with [AI chips leading](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA).

## Hold, trail, don't chase

With the swing ~+5% in profit and price reclaiming $210, the call is **HOLD at high conviction** — not chase. The one live risk is **FOMC on June 17**: at ~31x forward, a hawkish hold could pull NVDA back to test $205–$208 (now support), while a hold/dovish Fed likely extends the move toward **$220** and then the $235 ATH. Trail the stop up from $195 toward the $200 zone to bank the swing, keep the final add tranche dry for the post-FOMC resolution, and remember Juneteenth (June 19) thins liquidity into Friday. The plan worked; now manage the win.
